# Version 4.151.0
> **Performance and stability on Skia m151** · Released July 30, 2026 · [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/SkiaSharp/4.151.0) · [GitHub Release](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/releases/tag/v4.151.0)

> **API changes** · [SkiaSharp API diff](4.151.0/index.md) · [HarfBuzzSharp API diff](harfbuzzsharp/14.2.1/index.md)

## Highlights

SkiaSharp 4.151.0 brings Skia m151, broad managed-code performance wins, and a native resource leak fix. Across SKColor, SKPMColor, SKFourByteTag, HarfBuzzSharp buffers, and SKShaper glyph reads, hot-path allocations and P/Invoke round-trips have been replaced with managed integer math and zero-copy spans. A long-standing native resource leak in `SKImage.FromEncodedData` with a crop rect is also resolved.

## Breaking Changes

*None in this release.*

## Engine

- **Upgraded to Skia milestone m151** — The bundled Skia engine advances to m151, incorporating upstream rendering fixes, text improvements, and stability patches from multiple chrome/m151 sync merges. ([#4294](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4294), [#4312](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4312), [#4382](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4382), [#4443](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4443), [#4489](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4489))
- **CPU raster regression fixed** — A CPU raster rendering regression introduced in an earlier sync was resolved by restoring `SK_ENABLE_LEGACY_SHADERCONTEXT`. ([#4428](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4428))

## API Surface

- **`SKColor` gains `ReadOnlySpan<char>` hex overloads** — Parsing hex color strings now accepts `ReadOnlySpan<char>` in addition to `string`, avoiding allocations in hot parsing paths. Hex parsing itself was also made faster. ([#4345](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4345))
- **WASM: Emscripten 5.0.6 static libraries for .NET 11** — Pre-built WASM native assets compiled with Emscripten 5.0.6 (with the new `exnref` exception-handling ABI) are now included for .NET 11 targets. — ❤️ [@ramezgerges](https://github.com/ramezgerges) ([#4459](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4459), [#4487](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4487))

## Bug Fixes

- **Native resource leak in `SKImage.FromEncodedData` with crop rect fixed** — When `SKImage.FromEncodedData(SKData, SKRectI)` was called and decoding succeeded, the intermediate full image was never released. The handle is now freed correctly. ([#3997](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/3997))
- **Removed unnecessary `unsafe` modifier from `GRContextOptions`** — `GRContextOptions` no longer requires an `unsafe` compilation context; the surplus modifier has been removed. ([#3991](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/3991))

## Lifecycle & Internals

- **Hot-path P/Invoke eliminations across color and tag types** — `SKColor`↔`SKColorF` conversion, single-value `SKPMColor` premultiply/unpremultiply, and `SKFourByteTag.Parse` / `HarfBuzzSharp.Tag.Parse` are now pure managed integer math — no native calls on the hot path. ([#4370](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4370), [#4385](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4385), [#4396](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4396), [#4408](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4408))
- **SKShaper glyph results read via zero-copy spans** — The post-shaping glyph, cluster, and position arrays are now read directly from native memory via `Span<T>`, eliminating the intermediate managed array allocations on every `Shape` call. ([#4388](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4388))
- **HarfBuzzSharp `Buffer.AddUtf8(string)` made allocation-free** — The string-overload of `AddUtf8` now uses a pooled scratch buffer instead of allocating a `byte[]` per call, significantly reducing GC pressure in text-shaping loops. ([#4376](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4376))

## HarfBuzzSharp 14.2.1

HarfBuzzSharp 14.2.1 ships three performance improvements: `Buffer.AddUtf8(string)` is now allocation-free via buffer pooling, `Tag.Parse` eliminates its per-call `char[4]` allocation, and SKShaper reads glyph results through zero-copy spans.
